claim_verdicts.evidence: Kind opinion, taken from outline misconception 2; phrased as a consequence for the user, not as a documented rule. The 401/400/500 mapping it relies on is verified under claim 4.

issues.quote: The endpoint is marked `[Authorize]`, so the authentication middleware had already checked the `Authorization` header and recorded the caller before `Create` ran.
issues.text: Unlisted claim, and the causality is backwards. The authentication middleware (`app.UseAuthentication()`, default scheme JwtBearer) runs on every request whether or not the endpoint has `[Authorize]`. What `[Authorize]` adds is that authorization refuses a request with no authenticated user (challenge -> 401) before `Create` runs. ASP.NET Core docs: "Calling UseAuthentication registers the middleware that uses the previously registered authentication schemes."
issues.fix: Replace with: "The authentication middleware checks the `Authorization` header on every request and records the caller. Because `Create` is marked `[Authorize]`, a request without a valid token is answered `401` before `Create` runs." Keep the rest. Add a claim (kind behavior, version_key aspnetcore, source security/authentication/index.md).

issues.quote: A `POST` is not idempotent: sending the same request twice creates two orders.
issues.text: Unlisted claim. The statement is correct (RFC 9110 §9.2.2: "Of the request methods defined by this specification, PUT, DELETE, and safe request methods are idempotent."; lab: two identical POSTs created orders 29 and 30), but it is a specific HTTP-semantics claim that quiz q5 depends on, and it is missing from `claims`.
issues.fix: No text change needed. Add to meta.json claims: "POST is not idempotent (RFC 9110 §9.2.2); two identical POST /api/v1/orders create two orders", kind behavior, version_key http, section 4.

issues.quote: The Problem Details body the API sent, with its title and detail, is never read.
issues.text: Follows "Any other status becomes an exception", so it reads as if every failure carries Problem Details. A 401 from this API has no body at all (lab: `401`, `Content-Length: 0`, `Www-Authenticate: Bearer`); only the 400 and 500 paths write Problem Details.
issues.fix: Change to: "When the API sent a Problem Details body (as it does for `400` and `500`), its title and detail are never read."

issues.quote: Placing an order is a `POST` that creates a resource, so success is `201`, not `200`.
issues.text: Stated as an HTTP rule, but RFC 9110 §9.3.3 only says the origin server "SHOULD send a 201 (Created) response" when a POST created a resource. What is certain is this API's behaviour (CreatedAtAction -> 201, verified under claim 2).
issues.fix: Change to: "Placing an order is a `POST` that creates a resource, and this API answers it with `201 Created`, not `200`."
